title: The Deconvolver decides what is in a sample
set_out: Settle the cross-laboratory question on the 89 outside samples already read, each read as what the Deconvolver finds in it; keep every machine busy; then the Sequencing Atlas Globe page.
open_at_turnover: Google: Met-A synthetic test 3 and the class-floor synthetic. GitHub: R5 IBD blood, then R9 glioma, R5 sorted, R5 liver, R9 endothelial and the 100 spent healthy bloods on every atlas cell. Next: the per-person bar for the 100 bloods, the C-Score's atlas-only synthetic, lock 1 after the replays, the day summary.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: Megakaryocyte versions published
entries.what: IAM Sequencing Atlas version 1.1 and Sequencing Atlas Globe version 1.1 on Zenodo (the author's yes), 58 cells, the 57 unchanged.
entries.outcome: Live: 10.5281/zenodo.24029328 and 10.5281/zenodo.24029332; README, book, glossary, catalogue and site builders updated.
entries.reference: none (not a reading against healthy): a deposit of the atlas and globe

entries.title: What the chain reported on 89 outside samples
entries.what: Every outside-laboratory sequencing sample already read, tabulated from its bundle: the Deconvolver's cells, the library's false-call rate and depth.
entries.outcome: No sorted sample is one cell (the labeled cell 24 to 80 %); false-call rate 0.0016 to 0.0158 against the atlas laboratory's 0.0063.
entries.reference: none (not a reading against healthy): a table of what the chain reported

entries.title: The Deconvolver decides: synthetic
entries.what: Four arrays labeled sorted CD4, built as CD4, CD4 and monocytes, three cells, and all monocytes.
entries.outcome: Each read as what the Deconvolver found; the label flagged where it disagreed.
entries.reference: IAM-Atlas v2.1 (constructed arrays from its levels)

entries.title: Johns Hopkins tumor against the same person's non-tumor tissue
entries.what: Five people (three liver, two lung), all 12 tissues read at full depth on Google, each with its organ only as specimen.
entries.outcome: Whole-sample Met-A outside Normal in 2 of 5; the islands in 4 of 5 (met); IAM-A below Normal in 4 of 5 (recorded). The 'normal' is a cancer patient's non-tumor tissue (GEO), not healthy (author).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas for the untared readings; the scored bars divided tumor by the person's non-tumor tissue, which the atlas-only rule no longer allows (recorded)

entries.title: Naive and memory CD4 on sequencing: synthetic
entries.what: 30 constructed samples from the atlas's own subset columns, one per Google machine.
entries.outcome: Memory share within 0.07 at 15 and 40 reads a site; whether the columns' single donors stand for other people is the open part.
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (constructed samples from its columns)

entries.title: Cross-laboratory floor at the islands
entries.what: Each library's false-call floor read at the islands from the chain's own per-site tables.
entries.outcome: Outside libraries pass their whole floor to the islands, the atlas laboratory part of it; the domains read naive or memory cell state, not age.
entries.reference: none (not a reading against healthy): each library's own false-call floor

entries.title: Met-A healthy line: synthetic tests 3 to 5
entries.what: Test 3 over the real arrays' range (not met: the high tail's line measured from clipped anchors); test 4 with ten draws (not met; ran without its flag); test 5, the line measured with readings at 0 or 1 as censored, ten draws (met).
entries.outcome: Every condition's mean within 0.0010 of 1; the rehearsal on the 100 spent bloods is next.

entries.title: R5 Crohn's and colitis on every atlas cell
entries.what: 382 whole bloods and 240 sorted arrays of GSE87650 read again on every cell of IAM-Atlas v2.1.
entries.outcome: Whole blood: Crohn's against healthy differs in the cell mix (neutrophils 0.565 against 0.418) and a smoking site, not in Met-A; within each sorted cell type nothing separates disease from healthy.

entries.title: Met-A whole blood, the per-person rehearsal on the atlas alone
entries.what: The 100 spent healthy bloods of five laboratories read again on every atlas cell with the censored line, scored per person by the scorer sealed before the readings.
entries.outcome: Met: 98 of 100 inside Normal, every laboratory 18 to 20 of 20. Open: the ratio centers at 0.983 (the synthetic at 1.000), so a synthetic from the real full mix comes before the fresh test.

entries.title: The Deconvolver decides what is in a sample
entries.what: Four places where a label chose the cell removed (three in run_sample.py, one in run_series.py); the label is checked and recorded (label_check); gate rule 23b-h refuses any return; the lesson in the Decoder, the intake code and the workflow.
entries.outcome: Synthetic written before it runs (label_rule/label_synthetic.py).

entries.title: The atlases are the only healthy reference
entries.what: Author: healthy for comparisons always comes from the atlases. Gate rule 23b-i, design-check rules e and f (a Reference line naming an atlas; a bar per person), the commissioning check names every commissioning's reference; Met-A on neutrophils, the C-Score and Group-A (commissioned on a same-run tare) marked for re-commissioning on the atlas; the Decoder section.
entries.outcome: 45 control cases pass, including the real tare lines from this week's scorers.

entries.title: The Sequencing Atlas Globe page
entries.what: A page for each part of the globe beside its cosmology and genetics names, generated only from the story source.
entries.outcome: Committed; publishing waits on GitHub Pages.

entries.title: Merges save as they go
entries.what: Google merges save the merged molecules to the bucket the moment they exist and keep the chain's own log; dispatchers log GAVE UP and STUCK, which the loop check prints as failures.
entries.outcome: Found the five tumor merges' real stop: the specimen carried a status word.

entries.title: Lock 1, the reference door
entries.what: Every run of the one command checks IAM-Atlas v2.1 and the IAM Sequencing Atlas against their checksums before any reading, and every bundle records the atlases read and every tare applied.
entries.outcome: Synthetic met: a changed or unlisted atlas file stops the run before any reading; checked first on a fresh GitHub checkout.

sections.heading: What we learned that we did not know yesterday

entries.title: A tare looks like it works
entries.what: A sample divided by its neighbors comes out near 1 by construction: the same-laboratory tare put the medians at 1 while only 38 to 52 % of people read inside Normal.
entries.outcome: Bars are asked per person; the atlases are the only reference.

entries.title: Measure the real range before a synthetic
entries.what: Met-A's healthy-line synthetic missed on a weak array far more compressed than any of 331 real arrays the chain has measured; the formula itself is exact.
entries.outcome: Test 3 spans the real range; the weak array recorded, not scored.

entries.title: A patient's 'normal' tissue is not healthy
entries.what: GEO's matched normal is a cancer patient's non-tumor tissue.
entries.outcome: Tumors and their non-tumor tissue are both read against the atlas's healthy cells.

sections.heading: Our own mistakes, and what caught each

entries.title: A label chose the cell, inside the chain
entries.what: From 10-22 to 10-28 the agent added code that took the cell from the specimen's words (the sorted-cell Met-A, IAM-A's cell, a 'sorted X' override of the mix, a sample list's cell column), and the cross-laboratory scorers compared samples by label, against the author's 10-22 rule that the tools decide what is in a sample.
entries.outcome: Caught by the author; removed and refused by the gate (rule 23b-h).

entries.title: GitHub filled to the last slot
entries.what: The R12 every-cell replay was sent on 20 machines with R10 and R6 queued behind it, so the commit gate waited over 30 minutes, a lesson already given on 11-04.
entries.outcome: R10 and R6 cancelled before they started; every dispatch now leaves 2 slots free.

entries.title: Tares built on unchecked samples
entries.what: The same-laboratory tare, the Johns Hopkins CD4 tare and the tumor against own normal were designed against the agreement that the atlases are the ruler, and the array commissionings' same-run tare was never flagged.
entries.outcome: Code locks refuse each; three instruments marked for re-commissioning.

entries.title: Merges dropped without a word
entries.what: Five tumor merges failed three times each and the dispatcher logged 'waiting 0'; the half-hourly checks read machines busy, not results.
entries.outcome: GAVE UP and STUCK lines, printed as failures.

entries.title: A UTC time read as Pacific
entries.what: The author was told a stall began '3 AM yesterday' from a UTC machine-log stamp.
entries.outcome: Machine-log times converted to Pacific before quoting.

entries.title: A range stated wider than the data
entries.what: The tissue record said every sample read 1.20 to 1.36; one tumor reads 1.0416.
entries.outcome: Corrected before it reached GitHub.

entries.title: A flag that never reached arrays
entries.what: The censored-line flag was set only inside run_sample.py's sequencing branches, so synthetic test 4 on arrays ran the plain line.
entries.outcome: Found from the draws' recorded lines; the flag now set on every route; test 5's scorer refuses a draw whose line is not censored.

entries.title: Record edits erased by a commit in flight (a repeat)
entries.what: Test 3's result and test 4's design were written into the record while a commit was in flight; it refreshed the working copy and erased them, so test 4 ran without its design on record. The rule against editing during a commit was already on file from 11-02.
entries.outcome: Restored and disclosed (8cc58834); before any launch, the record, scripts and flag are checked on main.

entries.title: A Google machine idle for six hours
entries.what: The class-floor synthetic's job read the bucket name from a variable the machine never defines; under set -u it stopped at its first step, before the step that deletes the machine, and sat idle until its time limit. It was launched once, with no launcher watching it, and no check looked at whether a machine's log was moving.
entries.outcome: Path fixed; machine deleted; a stall check (a running machine whose log is unchanged for 45 minutes is a failure) added to the loop check; relaunched under a launcher.

entries.title: Two replays sent again that were already read on every cell
entries.what: R9 glioma blood and R5 liver cancer in blood were queued for every-cell reads although the replay record already holds both (r9_atlas_full, r5_atlas_full); the queue was chosen from the run registry, not the record.
entries.outcome: R9 glioma finished as a duplicate (not used); R5 liver cancelled within minutes. Lists are now checked against the record's summaries before queuing.
